Angus Place West coal mine extension - Reference 2022/09270

Say that the proposal is a controlled action.

All national heritage listed values identified by the Lithgow Environment Group submission should be assessed for the Angus Place West coal mine proposal. These values include:

  • 10 EPBC Listed Threatened Species and Ecological Communities;

  • 17 NSW BCA listed Threatened Species;

  • 2 EPBC Listed Migratory Species;

9.subject: Angus Place West mine - submission request update
9.body_html:
Please write a submission
 

Dear {contact.first_name}

Submissions close this Monday July 25th for the proposed Angus Place West coal mine in Gardens of Stone State Conservation Area. Help ensure Long Swamp and the swamps on Kangaroo and Lambs Creeks are adequately assessed under Federal environmental laws by making a submission. The mine would go under large upland swamps, including this one on Kangaroo Creek shown in the image above. 

I apologise to all who had their automated webform submission rejected by the Federal Environment Department. Last time I used this approach it worked, but the system has changed. All submissions already made through this website will be lodged on the EPBC Act Public Portal Monday afternoon. If you use the webform now it just records the data and I can lodge the submission later. Once again, sorry for the stuff up.

Please use the new system and write a submission through the EPBC Act Public Portal using the points below. You can add to these points by examining environment group submissions on the Gardens of Stone website.

Sincerely,

Keith Muir 0412791404

Send your submission on the Angus Place West mine proposal to the Federal Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water website. 

Start your submission with the tag line: 
Angus Place West coal mine extension - Reference 2022/09270

Use the points below to write a unique submission:

Say that the proposal is a controlled action.

All national heritage listed values identified by the Lithgow Environment Group submission should be assessed for the Angus Place West coal mine proposal. These values include:

  • 10 EPBC Listed Threatened Species and Ecological Communities;

  • 17 NSW BCA listed Threatened Species;

  • 2 EPBC Listed Migratory Species;

  • Significant Impacts on a Water Resource (Sydney drinking water catchment); and

  • Adverse impacts on World Heritage (Greater Blue Mountains  World Heritage Area (GBMWHA).

Federal regulators must ensure that environmental assessment for national heritage in the Angus Place West proposal include Long Swamp, and the swamps on Kangaroo and Lambs Creeks. 

These swamps were mapped as nationally endangered by independent experts using research funds provided by Centennial Coal as a result of an enforceable undertaking. This Federal Government compliance action required Centennial to pay $1.45 million following previous swamp damage at the Angus Place and Springvale mines. The independent research on these swamps should now inform the environmental assessments and Federal Government decisions for the Angus Place West proposal.
